question: Can permutation symmetry and clean-data quadratic mode connectivity remove diverse supervised and self-supervised image-model backdoors with little clean data, without reconstructing triggers or requiring labels?

key_findings.claim: Two-stage Symmetry Connectivity first sends a functionally identical copy of the compromised network to a deliberately anti-aligned neuron permutation, fits a clean-data Bezier path between the copies, and then realigns and reconnects an interior point to restore clean utility.
key_findings.evidence: The first permutation minimizes cross-model activation correlation while exactly preserving endpoint outputs; training the intervening curve only on clean samples empirically raises poisoned-sample loss near its interior. The second permutation maximizes correlation with the original basin and trains another clean-data curve. Algorithm 1 repeats this pair of operations with a short fine-tune between rounds.

key_findings.claim: Across the reported supervised matrix, TSC is the only evaluated method that keeps attack success below the authors' 15% success threshold for every listed CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and ImageNet-100 attack and poisoning-rate condition, at a nonzero clean-accuracy cost.
key_findings.evidence: For the difficult Blended attack, TSC reports 12.46% ASR and 91.12% ACC at 1% CIFAR-10 poisoning, versus 94.88% ASR and 93.76% ACC without defense; at 0.5% ImageNet-100 poisoning it reports 12.63% ASR and 76.58% ACC, versus 94.32% ASR and 84.44% ACC without defense. Other baselines often achieve better clean accuracy on selected attacks but fail the ASR threshold elsewhere.

anchors.section: Table 1 and 5.2 Results for Supervised Learning

key_findings.claim: The same mechanism directly purifies SimCLR and CLIP encoders and is materially more consistent than the original mode-connectivity repair on the tested downstream tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Under SimCLR BadEncoder attacks, the main text reports TSC below 11% ASR across all downstream tasks, while MCR fails on SVHN. Under the paper's CLIP setup, TSC reduces BadEncoder ASR below 2% across linear-probe and zero-shot tasks, whereas MCR is largely ineffective. The CLIP repair uses the full MS-COCO set rather than the 5% clean subset used in most other experiments and can lose accuracy on dissimilar domains.

anchors.section: Tables 2-3 and 5.3 Results for Self-supervised Learning
J Additional Results for Self-supervised Learning

key_findings.claim: A purpose-built symmetry-subspace adaptive attack does not defeat TSC in the authors' tests, but this is one white-box attack construction rather than evidence against all adaptive adversaries.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 4 jointly trains both endpoints and the connecting curve on mixed clean and poisoned data. TSC still lowers ASR across the reported supervised and SimCLR cases, and Figure 4 shows its benign-only first-stage curve entering a different high-poison-loss basin. The evaluation does not establish a worst-case adaptive guarantee or cover architectural backdoors excluded by the threat model.

key_findings.claim: The theorem orders selected upper bounds on curve loss; it does not prove that the actual poisoned-sample loss is larger after anti-alignment or that clean loss is smaller after realignment.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.2 propagates triangle and Lipschitz inequalities to produce UA,B <= UA,C under layerwise feature-distance and L2-norm-consistency assumptions. Corollary 4.3 therefore says anti-alignment can enlarge a loss upper bound. A looser upper bound alone does not order the underlying losses, and the trained Bezier deviations are assumed L2-norm-consistent rather than constrained to be so by Algorithm 1. The actual purification effect is empirical.

anchors.section: Corollary 4.3 and Increasing the Adversarial Loss

method.core_idea: Use a network's neuron-permutation orbit to manufacture distant, functionally identical endpoints whose clean-trained connecting path leaves the backdoor basin, then reconnect toward an aligned basin to regain utility.
method.mechanism: Clean activations define cross-correlation assignment matrices. A Hungarian solve selects minimum-correlation permutations for stage one and maximum-correlation permutations for stage two. Each pair of fixed endpoints is connected by a trainable quadratic Bezier curve whose control point is optimized using the original supervised, contrastive, or vision-language objective. An interior model is retrieved, lightly fine-tuned, and recycled for two or three global rounds.
assumptions: The defender has the compromised weights, the original basic training objective, enough compute to train several full-model curves, and a clean subset representative of the benign distribution.
The backdoor is encoded in an ordinary permutation-symmetric architecture rather than a malicious custom module.
Anti-aligning clean activations and fitting only clean data steers the curve away from the unknown trigger basin.
The L2-norm-consistency and Lipschitz assumptions used for the upper-bound theorem approximate the trained networks and Bezier deviations.

techniques.role: Uses a minimum-correlation assignment to select a far symmetry-equivalent endpoint without changing its predictions.
Trains a quadratic path on clean data so an interior point can leave the backdoor's low-loss region.
Maps the candidate back toward the original benign basin before a second curve recovers clean accuracy.
Repeats the two stages and light fine-tuning to trade progressively lower ASR for utility.
Trains a backdoored symmetry-connected curve to test whether the defense can route around an attack aware of its mechanism.

evaluations.setting: Supervised PreAct-ResNet18/ResNet50 models on CIFAR-10, GTSRB, and ImageNet-100 under eleven attack families and multiple poisoning rates.
evaluations.metric: Clean accuracy (ACC) and attack success rate (ASR), with ASR below 15% defined as successful defense.
evaluations.result: TSC reports sub-15% ASR in every table condition, including 12.46% on 1%-poisoned CIFAR-10 Blended and 12.63% on 0.5%-poisoned ImageNet-100 Blended, while sacrificing 2.64 and 7.86 ACC points respectively relative to no defense.
evaluations.baseline: No defense, fine-pruning, Neural Cleanse, MCR, ANP, FT-SAM, I-BAU, SAU, and selected additional methods.

evaluations.setting: BadEncoder and CTRL against SimCLR encoders, evaluated by downstream linear probes and selected KNN tasks.
evaluations.result: TSC remains below the paper's 15% ASR threshold across the listed tasks; MCR fails particularly on SVHN, while SSL-Cleanse is competitive in the SimCLR setting.
evaluations.baseline: Unrepaired encoder, MCR, SSL-Cleanse, and supplementary I-BAU/SAU adaptations.

evaluations.setting: BadEncoder applied to a CLIP ResNet50 visual encoder and repaired using MS-COCO, followed by linear-probe and zero-shot evaluation.
evaluations.metric: ACC and ASR on STL10, GTSRB, CIFAR-10, Food101, and VOC2007.
evaluations.result: TSC reports ASR below 2% throughout, but clean accuracy falls on several domains and improves on VOC2007, consistent with domain similarity to MS-COCO.

evaluations.setting: White-box subspace adaptive attacks, hyperparameter sweeps, alternative VGG19-BN/InceptionV3 architectures, and unpoisoned controls.
evaluations.metric: ACC-ASR tradeoff over global rounds and curve index, adaptive ASR, and clean-model accuracy drop.
evaluations.result: The tested adaptive construction remains mitigated; larger interior index and more rounds generally reduce ASR while lowering ACC; three supervised or two SSL rounds give the authors' preferred conservative settings.
evaluations.baseline: MCR and the same models before repair.

limitations: Author-stated: TSC sometimes trades clean accuracy for backdoor removal, and broader-scale validation remains future work.
Author-stated: the threat model excludes architectures containing dedicated malicious modules and assumes access to the original basic training procedure.
Reviewer inference: the mathematical result orders upper bounds rather than actual curve losses and relies on consistency assumptions not enforced by the algorithm.
Reviewer inference: CLIP uses the entire MS-COCO dataset and domain-dependent adaptation, so the claim of needing only a small clean fraction does not apply uniformly.
Reviewer inference: most tables do not report confidence intervals or seed-level variation; Figure 6 explicitly averages three runs, but broad statistical stability is not established.

Reviewer inference from the official repository: the release implements the paper's core loops but has no pinned dependency file or focused tests, and reproducing the matrix requires multiple external codebases, checkpoints, datasets, and substantial GPU training.
failure_modes: A clean subset with domain shift can make the curve forget benign features, as the CLIP discussion observes for GTSRB and CIFAR-10.
An architectural backdoor or non-permutation-symmetric malicious component falls outside the defense construction.
A stronger adaptive attacker may distribute malicious behavior across many symmetry basins or target the benign-only curve objective itself.
Poorly chosen curve index or too few global rounds leaves high ASR; overly aggressive settings erase clean utility.
Architectures requiring hand-written channel-permutation plumbing can be unsupported or incorrectly permuted around residual, normalization, or attention structure.
reusable_insights: A model's symmetry orbit can provide function-preserving endpoints for security interventions without first recovering an unknown trigger.
Report the full Pareto curve between clean utility and attack success; a single ASR threshold hides materially different tradeoffs.
For any theorem based on ordered upper bounds, separately test whether the measured quantity itself is ordered and enforce the theorem's structural assumptions in code.
Encoder repair should be evaluated before and after downstream adaptation, across domains both similar to and distant from the repair data.
Adaptive evaluation should target the defense's routing mechanism, but one mechanistic attack is a lower bound on adversarial coverage, not a certificate.
open_questions: Can actual poisoned-loss separation be proved rather than only separation of selectable upper bounds?
Can curve endpoints or indices be selected without any trigger knowledge while providing a prospective clean-utility guarantee?
How does symmetry-connectivity repair scale to transformers, vision transformers, mixture-of-experts, and normalization schemes with more complicated invariances?
Can an attacker train a backdoor that remains low loss across a large sample of anti-aligned permutations and benign-data curves?
Does a small, fixed, out-of-domain public dataset suffice for foundation-model repair without domain-specific forgetting?

competitive_landscape.title: Bridging Mode Connectivity in Loss Landscapes and Adversarial Robustness
competitive_landscape.difference: MCR repairs tampered models by training a low-clean-loss path between independently obtained endpoints. TSC adds deliberate symmetry anti-alignment and a second realigned path, addressing cases where an ordinary connection remains inside the backdoor basin.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Stable Backdoor Purification through Feature Shift Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: Feature Shift Tuning deliberately moves classifier features away from compromised weights in about ten fine-tuning epochs and targets low-poison-rate entanglement. TSC is more training-format general but trains multiple 200-epoch curves and requires architecture-aware permutations.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Fine-Tuning Based Backdoor Defense with Sharpness-Aware Minimization
competitive_landscape.difference: FT-SAM shrinks high-norm backdoor-related neurons through supervised sharpness-aware fine-tuning. TSC avoids a neuron-norm backdoor assumption and transfers to SSL objectives, at substantially greater path-training cost.

competitive_landscape.title: SSL-Cleanse: Trojan Detection and Mitigation in Self-Supervised Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: SSL-Cleanse clusters unlabeled representations, reverses a trigger, and unlearns it, providing both detection and mitigation without known downstream tasks. TSC does not detect or reconstruct triggers and extends one mechanism across supervised, SimCLR, and CLIP training, but assumes a clean repair set and training objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Backdoor Defense through Self-Supervised and Generative Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Sabolić et al. fit class-conditional generative models in self-supervised feature space to detect poisoned training data and retrain on a cleansed set. TSC instead repairs weights post hoc without identifying poisoned examples, including settings where the original training data are unavailable.

competitive_landscape.title: The Platonic Defense: Backdoor Defense for Self-Supervised Encoders in the Era of Large Scale Pre-training
competitive_landscape.difference: The 2026 Platonic Defense uses reference encoders and an energy model for black-box test-time detection and representation purification across more than ten attacks. It relaxes TSC's access to model weights and training procedure, while adding dependence on trusted reference representations and learned energy estimation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first robust data-format-independent purification framework that exploits weight symmetry plus quadratic connectivity across supervised, SimCLR, and CLIP settings, with theoretical loss-bound analysis and adaptive-attack robustness.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The two-stage algorithm combines anti-aligned and aligned permutation assignments with learned Bezier paths; the experiments span eleven supervised attacks, two SSL attacks, multiple architectures, adaptive variants, and clean controls.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The novel contribution is the anti-align/connect/realign/connect routing mechanism and its unusually broad empirical application, not mode connectivity, weight matching, or clean-data purification individually. The theoretical language should be narrowed: the proof explains ordering of constructed bounds, while the evidence that poisoned loss actually rises and ASR falls comes from experiments.

reviewer_notes: Read all 37 extracted pages and audited all 15 figures, 19 tables, four algorithms, theorem proofs, trigger examples, full attack/defense settings, and references. The official GitHub release was checked: its supervised and SSL scripts implement iterative minimum-/maximum-correlation Hungarian permutations and fixed-endpoint curve training, but the repository has only two commits, no pinned environment, and no focused TSC tests; no full rerun was attempted because the paper uses many external datasets/checkpoints and V100-scale training. Six primary arXiv competitors, including a June 2026 black-box SSL defense, were checked on 2026-08-23. The material contradiction is that a larger valid upper bound does not itself prove a larger realized loss.
